outcome: No result advancing the Bass conjecture (finite generation of K_i(X) for regular schemes X of finite type over Z, or equivalently K_n(A) for regular finitely generated Z-algebras A) was found in the window 26 January 2024 to present. Quillen's dimension-≤1 case remains the frontier result; higher-dimensional cases remain open.
summary: Extensive searching across arXiv, Wikipedia, and general web sources turned up nothing that advances this specific conjecture — Bass's conjecture that K_i(X) (or K'_i(X), or the motivic-cohomology refinement H^i_M(X,Z(n))) is finitely generated for regular schemes X of finite type over Z — in the window since 26 January 2024. The known state remains what it was before the window: Quillen proved the dimension ≤1 case (curves over finite fields, rings of integers in number fields) decades ago, and the case CH_0(X) (zero-cycles) follows from higher-dimensional class field theory, also pre-2024. Higher-dimensional cases remain open, as confirmed by Geisser's survey on finite generation questions for motivic cohomology and by the current Wikipedia article on the Bass conjecture, neither of which records any post-2024 development. Every search that surfaced 'Bass' and 'K-theory' together in 2024-2025 preprints (e.g. arXiv:2512.18868, arXiv:2503.10163) concerned the distinct Bass–Quillen conjecture on finitely generated projective modules over regular rings, which is a different question about projective modules, not about finite generation of K-groups as abelian groups — this matches the triage's finding and I confirm the triage was right to treat those as out of scope (§3.1: a different problem sharing a namesake, not a case or restriction of this one). No AI system appears anywhere in the material found, unsurprising given that nothing at all was found to attribute it to.
competing_reading: One could argue that any of the many papers on finiteness of related invariants (unramified cohomology, higher Chow groups, motivic cohomology of specific varieties over finite fields) constitute 'partial progress' if they establish finite generation for some class of X not previously known. I did not find any such paper dated within the window that goes beyond what was already known pre-2024 (e.g. arXiv:2302.09867 on motivic cohomology of surfaces over finite fields appears to be older/pre-window work reappearing in searches, and arXiv:2309.08463 and arXiv:2605.22494 concern equicharacteristic/Bloch-Ogus phenomena rather than establishing new finite-generation results for the arithmetic (mixed-characteristic) schemes this bullet concerns). If a hidden, more targeted result exists in a paper I did not surface, this would need reclassifying, but nothing found supports it.
what_would_settle_it: A paper explicitly proving finite generation of K_i(X) or K'_i(X) for some new class of regular schemes X of finite type over Z beyond dimension ≤1 (or of the refined motivic-cohomology groups H^i_M(X,Z(n))), dated after 26 January 2024, with an abstract or introduction that states the result as advancing Bass's finiteness conjecture specifically (not the Bass-Quillen projective-module conjecture).
